title: Vision and Mission Endings
kidRule: A buzzy 'zhun' ending, like in VISION, is almost always spelled S-I-O-N. A hushed 'shun' ending is sometimes spelled with S too, and after a short vowel it is usually S-S-I-O-N, like in MISSION.
hint: Listen to the ending. Is it a buzzy 'zhun' or a hushed 'shun'? It is not spelled the way it sounds, so think about which letters make that ending.
reminder: This ending is spelled S-I-O-N, and sometimes it needs a double S: S-S-I-O-N. If your first try did not work, try the other!

check.question: Why does VISION end with S-I-O-N?
check.correctAnswer: Because the buzzy 'zhun' sound at the end of a word is spelled S-I-O-N!
distractors: Because S-I-O-N is only used in words about seeing
Because the letter Z is never allowed in a long word

words.def: An important job that someone is sent to do.
words.sent: The astronauts trained for their mission to the moon.
words.story: The Apollo 11 mission in 1969 was the first to land people on the moon!
words.card: Don't *miss* the secret *mission* to rescue the last cupcake!

words.def: The power to see with your eyes.
words.sent: An owl has amazing vision in the dark.
words.story: Eagles have vision so sharp that they can spot a rabbit from about two miles away!
words.card: My *vision* *is* so good that I can see a flea wearing socks!

words.def: A machine with a screen that shows moving pictures with sound.
words.sent: We watched a cartoon on the television after dinner.
words.story: The first part of the word, 'tele', means far away, so the whole word really means seeing from far away!
words.card: I used a *tele*scope to watch *television* from the treehouse!

words.def: A sudden, very loud burst when something blows apart.
words.sent: The fireworks made a colorful explosion in the sky.
words.story: In 1883 the volcano Krakatoa made an explosion so loud that people heard it almost 3,000 miles away!
words.card: The popcorn made a tiny *explosion* and went *plo*p into my hat!

words.def: A talk where people share their ideas about something.
words.sent: Our class had a discussion about which pet is best.
words.story: Honeybees have their own kind of discussion: scout bees dance to show where a new home could be, and the swarm picks the favorite!
words.card: Come sit with *us* for a *discussion* about why penguins never wear pajamas!

words.def: A very big, fancy house with lots of rooms.
words.sent: The old mansion on the hill had fifty windows.
words.story: The White House, where the president of the United States lives, is a mansion with 132 rooms and 35 bathrooms!
words.card: A snow*man* moved into the *mansion* and filled every room with ice cream!

words.def: A choice you make after thinking about it.
words.sent: Picking the red bike was an easy decision.
words.story: At the start of a football game, a coin is flipped to help make the very first decision: which team gets to choose first!
words.card: I made a *decision* to put ketchup *on* my ice cream. Yuck!

words.def: The mixed-up feeling when you do not understand what is happening.
words.sent: There was confusion when two teachers rang the bell at once.
words.story: A group of wildebeest is sometimes called a confusion!
words.card: The *con*fetti cannon caused *confusion* at the cat's birthday party!

words.def: When someone says yes, you are allowed to do something.
words.sent: Dad gave us permission to stay up late.
words.story: At a big airport, a pilot must get permission from the control tower before the plane can take off or land!
words.card: I have *permission* to wear my su*per*hero cape to the dentist!

words.def: Something that tricks your eyes so it looks different from what is really there.
words.sent: The magician's floating card was only an illusion.
words.story: The moon looks bigger when it is low in the sky than when it is high up, but it is really the same size. That trick is called the Moon illusion!
words.card: The *ill* wizard sneezed and his best *illusion* turned into a duck!
